claims.text: Thermal annealing of as-synthesized nanoscale PtPdRhRuIrOs solid-solution catalysts improves ethanol oxidation activity.
Thermal annealing reduces surface compositional fluctuations and eliminates deleterious segregation.
Reduced compositional fluctuations and segregation fine-tune the d-band center of active sites.
The initial nanoscale PtPdRhRuIrOs catalysts are produced by rapid quenching.
The as-synthesized catalysts have a homogeneous but kinetically trapped atomic distribution.
Minor local segregation may arise during synthesis.
The controlled change is thermal annealing under an inert or reducing atmosphere at a temperature and duration selected to avoid sintering.
Atomic ordering and surface homogeneity modulate the local d-band center of catalytically active sites.
Annealing produces a more uniform electronic structure with an optimized d-band center.
An optimized d-band center enhances the adsorption energetics of ethanol and its reaction intermediates.
Enhanced adsorption energetics increase ethanol oxidation activity.
Under identical electrochemical testing conditions, the annealed catalyst will have a higher ethanol oxidation current density than the untreated catalyst.
The appropriate baseline is the as-synthesized nanoscale PtPdRhRuIrOs catalyst without post-synthesis thermal treatment.
The proposed effect requires an annealing temperature high enough to promote atomic homogenization but low enough to avoid sintering or phase separation.
The proposed effect is expected under typical ethanol oxidation electrochemical conditions.
Failure to obtain a statistically significant current-density improvement, or failure to observe the corresponding structural or electronic change, would falsify the hypothesis.
